The Reporter (COMP-008 / T03.13) enforces the\n29\t   N'-vs-K invariant on top of this — the orchestrator never elides a\n30\t   spec.\n31\t3. **Cooperative cancellation.** When a shared\n32\t   :class:`CancellationToken` is wired (NFR-REL1 / T03.07), the\n33\t   orchestrator stops submitting new work as soon as it observes the\n34\t   token cancelled. Specs that were never submitted synthesise an\n35\t   ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome at the orchestrator layer so the per-spec\n36\t   contract still holds.  In-flight runners observe the same token via\n37\t   :class:`EvalRunner` and convert worker-thread\n38\t   ``KeyboardInterrupt`` / ``SystemExit`` into ``INTERRUPTED`` outcomes\n39\t   themselves — the orchestrator never has to translate an exception\n40\t   into a status.\n41\t\n42\tThe orchestrator deliberately does *not* install signal handlers. Building an :class:`EvalRunner` requires per-eval HOME\n53\tisolation, scratch paths, executor wiring, and an expect-callable\n54\tsequence — none of which the orchestrator can resolve. Computed once at import time so\nthe helper does not re-derive it on every call.\n\"\"\"\n\nRAM_CEILING_TEXT: str = f\"{RAM_CEILING_GB} GB\"\n\"\"\"Canonical rendering of the ceiling used in operator-facing strings.\n\nThe T03.17 AC asserts that the warning contains this literal token. Pin\nit here so any downstream string formatting picks up changes uniformly.\n\"\"\"\n\nPARALLEL_RAM_GATE_THRESHOLD: int = 15\n\"\"\"``--parallel`` value at-or-above which the RAM precheck fires.\n\nMatches :attr:`RunOrchestrator.MAX_PARALLEL`. Below this threshold the\nbenchmark does not document a ceiling, so the doctor stays silent rather\nthan emit a misleading number.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _default_free_ram_probe() -> Optional[int]:\n    \"\"\"Return free RAM in bytes via Linux ``/proc/meminfo``.\n\n    Prefers ``MemAvailable`` (kernel ≥3.14) because it accounts for\n    reclaimable cache the way an oncoming allocation would; falls back to\n    ``MemFree`` on ancient kernels. hosts is worse than one that warns.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    meminfo = Path(\"/proc/meminfo\")\n    if not meminfo.is_file():\n        return None\n    try:\n        text = meminfo.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    except OSError:\n        return None\n    available: Optional[int] = None\n    free: Optional[int] = None\n    for line in text.splitlines():\n        key, _, rest = line.partition(\":\")\n        key = key.strip()\n        if key not in (\"MemAvailable\", \"MemFree\"):\n            continue\n        tokens = rest.strip().split()\n        if not tokens:\n            continue\n        try:\n            kb = int(tokens[0])\n        except ValueError:\n            continue\n        unit = tokens[1].lower() if len(tokens) > 1 else \"kb\"\n        # /proc/meminfo always reports in kB on Linux; the unit check is\n        # defensive in case a future kernel changes the format.\n        multiplier = 1024 if unit == \"kb\" else 1\n        value = {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_01NrvUA15Zq4AzBwFN4GaErr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01S4mGuC6FF44YE9z6jBuEyg","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/config/workspace/IronClaude/src/superclaude/cli/eval/disk_budget.py","content":"\"\"\"NFR-PERF4 disk-budget poller (T03.19 / D-0060 / R-060).\n\nDesign-spec §4 (``--max-disk-mb``) and §13 (NFR-PERF4) require the\norchestrator to bound the cumulative artifact size under\n``--output-dir`` during a run. The motivation is the R4 risk row in\ndesign-spec §10: a fan-out of 15 concurrent HOMEs with PTY transcripts\ncan grow past several hundred megabytes on a slow eval; left unchecked,\nthat fills the developer host (or a CI runner with a tight disk quota)\nand corrupts every neighbouring run. The orchestrator addresses this\nby polling the run-directory size every five seconds and signalling a\n\"stop scheduling, drain in-flight, exit 2\" breach when the configured\nbudget is exceeded.\n\nThis module implements the polling primitive. The integration with\n:class:`RunOrchestrator` lives in ``orchestrator.py``; the CLI flag\n(``--max-disk-mb``) is wired by the Phase 4 dispatcher per design-spec\n§4. The poller is deliberately decoupled from both so it can be exercised\nin isolation by the T03.19 fixture suite (``test_disk_budget.py``) and\nre-used by any future component (eg. the doctor pre-flight) that needs\na cheap, side-effect-free disk gauge.\n\nPublic surface\n==============\n\n:class:`DiskBudgetPoller`\n    Background-thread poller. Constructed with an output directory and a\n    ``max_disk_mb`` budget; ``start()`` / ``stop()`` (or the context-\n    manager form) drive the background thread. Exposes :meth:`is_breached`\n    so the orchestrator can short-circuit its submission loop and\n    :meth:`breach_detail` for the partial-summary payload.\n\n:data:`DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE`\n    Process exit code emitted by the Phase 4 dispatcher when the poller\n    has flagged a breach. ``2`` per design-spec §4 (harness error).\n\n:data:`DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`\n    Filename of the side-car the poller writes inside the run directory\n    on breach. The Reporter (COMP-008 / T03.13) surfaces this path under\n    ``RunSummary.artifacts['disk_budget_exceeded']``; the filename is\n    pinned here so consumers do not have to discover it by scan.\n\nBreach semantics\n================\n\nWhen ``max_disk_mb > 0``:\n\n* The poller measures cumulative size of the output directory tree every\n  ``tick_sec`` seconds (default ``5.0``). The first tick fires *after*\n  the initial sleep so an empty run directory does not get flagged on\n  start-up.\n* When measured usage exceeds ``max_disk_mb * 1024 * 1024`` bytes, the\n  poller writes ``DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`` into the output\n  directory, sets its internal ``is_breached()`` flag, and exits the\n  loop. The flag is one-shot — once set, the poller stays in the\n  breached state for the rest of its lifetime.\n* The orchestrator polls ``is_breached()`` between submissions; on a\n  breach it stops scheduling new specs and synthesises a\n  ``SKIPPED`` outcome (skip_reason ``\"disk_budget_exceeded\"``) for every\n  unsubmitted spec. In-flight workers continue to completion — the\n  poller never kills a thread or sends a signal.\n\nWhen ``max_disk_mb == 0``:\n\n* The poller is *disabled*. ``start()`` is a no-op, the background\n  thread is never spawned, and :meth:`is_breached` always returns\n  ``False``. The orchestrator behaves as if no poller were wired.\n  Design-spec §4 documents ``--max-disk-mb 0`` as the \"disable\"\n  invocation.\n\nThread safety\n=============\n\nThe breach state is stored as a :class:`threading.Event`. Reading the\ndetail mapping after :meth:`is_breached` returns ``True`` is safe because\nthe detail is published *before* the event is set (release-then-set\nordering). The poller thread is the only writer of the detail; the\norchestrator (main) thread is the only reader. Both ends communicate\nthrough the event without explicit locking.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Mapping, Optional\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME\",\n    \"DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE\",\n    \"DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_REASON\",\n    \"DEFAULT_DISK_BUDGET_MB\",\n    \"DEFAULT_DISK_POLL_TICK_SEC\",\n    \"DiskBudgetPoller\",\n]\n\n\n# Process exit code returned by the Phase 4 CLI dispatcher when the\n# poller has signalled a breach. Matches the design-spec §4 exit-code\n# table: ``2`` = harness error. The disk-budget breach is a harness-\n# enforced abort, not a per-eval failure, so it uses the same code as\n# the loader / scratch-root / reporter-contract violations.\nDISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE: int = 2\n\n# Filename the poller writes when a breach is detected. Pinned here so\n# the orchestrator, Reporter, and integration tests all reference one\n# constant. ``.json`` because the payload is a structured\n# :class:`BreachDetail` projection.\nDISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME: str = \"disk_budget_exceeded.json\"\n\n# ``skip_reason`` token written into every synthesised SKIPPED outcome\n# the orchestrator emits for unsubmitted specs after a breach. The motivation is the R4 risk row in\ndesign-spec §10: a fan-out of 15 concurrent HOMEs with PTY transcripts\ncan grow past several hundred megabytes on a slow eval; left unchecked,\nthat fills the developer host (or a CI runner with a tight disk quota)\nand corrupts every neighbouring run. The integration with\n15\t:class:`RunOrchestrator` lives in ``orchestrator.py``; the CLI flag\n16\t(``--max-disk-mb``) is wired by the Phase 4 dispatcher per design-spec\n17\t§4. The poller is deliberately decoupled from both so it can be exercised\n18\tin isolation by the T03.19 fixture suite (``test_disk_budget.py``) and\n19\tre-used by any future component (eg. the doctor pre-flight) that needs\n20\ta cheap, side-effect-free disk gauge.\n21\t\n22\tPublic surface\n23\t==============\n24\t\n25\t:class:`DiskBudgetPoller`\n26\t    Background-thread poller. Exposes :meth:`is_breached`\n29\t    so the orchestrator can short-circuit its submission loop and\n30\t    :meth:`breach_detail` for the partial-summary payload.\n31\t\n32\t:data:`DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE`\n33\t    Process exit code emitted by the Phase 4 dispatcher when the poller\n34\t    has flagged a breach. ``2`` per design-spec §4 (harness error).\n35\t\n36\t:data:`DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`\n37\t    Filename of the side-car the poller writes inside the run directory\n38\t    on breach. The Reporter (COMP-008 / T03.13) surfaces this path under\n39\t    ``RunSummary.artifacts['disk_budget_exceeded']``; the filename is\n40\t    pinned here so consumers do not have to discover it by scan.\n41\t\n42\tBreach semantics\n43\t================\n44\t\n45\tWhen ``max_disk_mb > 0``:\n46\t\n47\t* The poller measures cumulative size of the output directory tree every\n48\t  ``tick_sec`` seconds (default ``5.0``). The first tick fires *after*\n49\t  the initial sleep so an empty run directory does not get flagged on\n50\t  start-up.\n51\t* When measured usage exceeds ``max_disk_mb * 1024 * 1024`` bytes, the\n52\t  poller writes ``DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`` into the output\n53\t  directory, sets its internal ``is_breached()`` flag, and exits the\n54\t  loop. The flag is one-shot — once set, the poller stays in the\n55\t  breached state for the rest of its lifetime.\n56\t* The orchestrator polls ``is_breached()`` between submissions; on a\n57\t  breach it stops scheduling new specs and synthesises a\n58\t  ``SKIPPED`` outcome (skip_reason ``\"disk_budget_exceeded\"``) for every\n59\t  unsubmitted spec. In-flight workers continue to completion — the\n60\t  poller never kills a thread or sends a signal.\n61\t\n62\tWhen ``max_disk_mb == 0``:\n63\t\n64\t* The poller is *disabled*. ``start()`` is a no-op, the background\n65\t  thread is never spawned, and :meth:`is_breached` always returns\n66\t  ``False``. The motivation is the R4 risk row in\ndesign-spec §10: a fan-out of 15 concurrent HOMEs with PTY transcripts\ncan grow past several hundred megabytes on a slow eval; left unchecked,\nthat fills the developer host (or a CI runner with a tight disk quota)\nand corrupts every neighbouring run. The orchestrator addresses this\nby polling the run-directory size every five seconds and signalling a\n\"stop scheduling, drain in-flight, exit 2\" breach when the configured\nbudget is exceeded.\n\nThis module implements the polling primitive. The integration with\n:class:`RunOrchestrator` lives in ``orchestrator.py``; the CLI flag\n(``--max-disk-mb``) is wired by the Phase 4 dispatcher per design-spec\n§4. Constructed with an output directory and a\n    ``max_disk_mb`` budget; ``start()`` / ``stop()`` (or the context-\n    manager form) drive the background thread. The Reporter (COMP-008 / T03.13) surfaces this path under\n    ``RunSummary.artifacts['disk_budget_exceeded']``; the filename is\n    pinned here so consumers do not have to discover it by scan.\n\nBreach semantics\n================\n\nWhen ``max_disk_mb > 0``:\n\n* The poller measures cumulative size of the output directory tree every\n  ``tick_sec`` seconds (default ``5.0``). The first tick fires *after*\n  the initial sleep so an empty run directory does not get flagged on\n  start-up.\n* When measured usage exceeds ``max_disk_mb * 1024 * 1024`` bytes, the\n  poller writes ``DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`` into the output\n  directory, sets its internal ``is_breached()`` flag, and exits the\n  loop. The flag is one-shot — once set, the poller stays in the\n  breached state for the rest of its lifetime.\n* The orchestrator polls ``is_breached()`` between submissions; on a\n  breach it stops scheduling new specs and synthesises a\n  ``SKIPPED`` outcome (skip_reason ``\"disk_budget_exceeded\"``) for every\n  unsubmitted spec. In-flight workers continue to completion — the\n  poller never kills a thread or sends a signal.\n\nWhen ``max_disk_mb == 0``:\n\n* The poller is *disabled*. ``start()`` is a no-op, the background\n  thread is never spawned, and :meth:`is_breached` always returns\n  ``False``. The implementation deliberately\nmirrors the shape used by ``src/superclaude/cli/prd/executor.py:774-802``\nso a reader switching between the PRD pipeline and the eval harness sees\nthe same scheduling skeleton.\n\nResponsibilities\n================\n\nThe orchestrator owns three cross-cutting concerns the lifecycle layer\nintentionally defers:\n\n1. **Concurrency budget.** ``max_workers`` is clamped to ``[1, 15]`` per\n   design-spec §11 (NFR-PERF2) with a default of ``8``. Values outside\n   the range either raise (``parallel < 1``) or saturate to the upper\n   bound (``parallel > 15``). The clamp is enforced once at the top of\n   :meth:`RunOrchestrator.run` so the rest of the body can trust the\n   effective value.\n2. **Outcome contract.** :class:`RunOrchestrator` guarantees one\n   :class:`EvalOutcome` per input :class:`EvalSpec` in the original\n   sequence order. The Reporter (COMP-008 / T03.13) enforces the\n   N'-vs-K invariant on top of this — the orchestrator never elides a\n   spec.\n3. **Cooperative cancellation.** When a shared\n   :class:`CancellationToken` is wired (NFR-REL1 / T03.07), the\n   orchestrator stops submitting new work as soon as it observes the\n   token cancelled. Specs that were never submitted synthesise an\n   ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome at the orchestrator layer so the per-spec\n   contract still holds.  In-flight runners observe the same token via\n   :class:`EvalRunner` and convert worker-thread\n   ``KeyboardInterrupt`` / ``SystemExit`` into ``INTERRUPTED`` outcomes\n   themselves — the orchestrator never has to translate an exception\n   into a status.\n\nThe orchestrator deliberately does *not* install signal handlers. Signal\ninstallation is the CLI dispatcher's job (Phase 4): the dispatcher\nallocates a :class:`CancellationToken`, wraps the orchestrator call in a\n:class:`SignalHandlerInstaller`, and hands the token down so the eval\nrunners observe the same cancellation flag the signal handler flips.\n\nWorker contract\n===============\n\nThe orchestrator does not construct :class:`EvalRunner` instances\nitself. Building an :class:`EvalRunner` requires per-eval HOME\nisolation, scratch paths, executor wiring, and an expect-callable\nsequence — none of which the orchestrator can resolve. Values outside\n   the range either raise (``parallel < 1``) or saturate to the upper\n   bound (``parallel > 15``). The clamp is enforced once at the top of\n   :meth:`RunOrchestrator.run` so the rest of the body can trust the\n   effective value.\n2. **Outcome contract.** :class:`RunOrchestrator` guarantees one\n   :class:`EvalOutcome` per input :class:`EvalSpec` in the original\n   sequence order. Specs that were never submitted synthesise an\n   ``INTERRUPTED`` outcome at the orchestrator layer so the per-spec\n   contract still holds. Building an :class:`EvalRunner` requires per-eval HOME\nisolation, scratch paths, executor wiring, and an expect-callable\nsequence — none of which the orchestrator can resolve. Goal\n9\t\n10\tSchedule per-spec `EvalRunner` workers in parallel via\n11\t`concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor + as_completed` — the AC6\n12\tpattern the cliEval design-spec pins (referenced shape:\n13\t`src/superclaude/cli/prd/executor.py:774-802`). The orchestrator owns\n14\tthree cross-cutting concerns the lifecycle layer (T03.04) and runner\n15\tclass (T03.05) deliberately deferred:\n16\t\n17\t1. **Concurrency budget** — `max_workers` clamped to `[1, 15]` per\n18\t   design-spec §11 / NFR-PERF2 with default `8`.\n19\t2. **Outcome contract** — one `EvalOutcome` per input `EvalSpec`, in\n20\t   input order, regardless of completion order (the Reporter / FR-RPT1\n21\t   N'-vs-K invariant relies on this).\n22\t3. **Cooperative cancellation** — when the shared `CancellationToken`\n23\t   (NFR-REL1 / T03.07) flips, scheduling stops and unsubmitted specs\n24\t   synthesise an `INTERRUPTED` outcome so the per-spec contract still\n25\t   holds.\n26\t\n27\tThe orchestrator does **not** install signal handlers. Keeping the orchestrator agnostic of construction\n49\tdetails lets the CLI dispatcher own resource allocation and lets tests\n50\tsubstitute a stub worker that returns a canned outcome.\n51\t\n52\t### 2.2 `RunOrchestrator`\n53\t\n54\t| Attribute / method | Contract |\n55\t|---|---|\n56\t| `DEFAULT_PARALLEL: ClassVar[int] = 8` | Default concurrency level. |\n57\t| `MIN_PARALLEL: ClassVar[int] = 1` | Minimum accepted `parallel`. Values below raise `ValueError`. |\n58\t| `MAX_PARALLEL: ClassVar[int] = 15` | Upper bound; values above saturate. |\n59\t| `__init__(*, run_one, cancellation_token=None)` | Worker callable + optional token. Non-callable `run_one` raises `TypeError`. |\n60\t| `run(specs, *, parallel=DEFAULT_PARALLEL) -> list[EvalOutcome]` | Schedule and collect outcomes. Empty `specs` → `[]`. |\n61\t\n62\t### 2.3 Outcome shape\n63\t\n64\tThe orchestrator emits two synthesised outcome shapes itself:\n65\t\n66\t| Shape | Trigger | Status | `duration_sec` | `error_class` |\n67\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n68\t| Interrupted | Cancellation token set before spec submitted | `INTERRUPTED` | `0.0` | `None` |\n69\t| Errored | Worker callable raised | `ERRORED` | `0.0` | `f\"{type(exc).__module__}.{type(exc).__qualname__}\"` |\n70\t\n71\tEvery other outcome shape is returned verbatim from the worker —\n72\tnotably `PASS` / `FAIL` / `TIMEOUT` / `INTERRUPTED` from the in-runner\n73\tclassification (D-0049 / D-0050).\n74\t\n75\t## 3. Scheduling Pattern\n76\t\n77\t```python\n78\twith ThreadPoolExecutor(\n79\t    max_workers=max_workers, thread_name_prefix=\"cliEval\"\n80\t) as pool:\n81\t    futures: dict[Future[EvalOutcome], int] = {}\n82\t    for index, spec in enumerate(specs):\n83\t        if self._is_cancelled():\n84\t            cancelled_indices.append(index)\n85\t            continue\n86\t        futures[pool.submit(self._invoke_worker, spec)] = index\n87\t\n88\t    for future in as_completed(futures):\n89\t        index = futures[future]\n90\t        try:\n91\t            outcomes[index] = future.result()\n92\t        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n93\t            outcomes[index] = self._errored_outcome(specs[index], exc)\n94\t\n95\tfor index in cancelled_indices:\n96\t    outcomes[index] = self._interrupted_outcome(specs[index])\n97\t```\n98\t\n99\tNotes:\n100\t\n101\t* `outcomes` is pre-allocated and indexed by submission order so the\n102\t  return-value order is independent of completion order.\n103\t* The cancellation check is per-spec inside the submission loop, not\n104\t  per-future. In-flight runners observe the same token via\n105\t  `EvalRunner._cancellation_token` (D-0050) and convert worker-thread\n106\t  `KeyboardInterrupt` / `SystemExit` into `INTERRUPTED` outcomes\n107\t  themselves — the orchestrator never has to translate an exception\n108\t  into a status.\n109\t* `thread_name_prefix=\"cliEval\"` makes per-eval threads identifiable in\n110\t  `py-spy` / `ps` output for diagnosing hangs.\n111\t\n112\t## 4. Parallelism Validation\n113\t\n114\t`tests/cli/eval/test_orchestrator.py::test_three_eval_suite_runs_faster_than_3x_sequential`\n115\tasserts the runtime contract directly:\n116\t\n117\t* 3 specs × 0.2s sleep each.\n118\t* `parallel=3`.\n119\t* Elapsed must be `< 3 × eval_duration_sec` (i.e. `< 0.6s`). Goal\n\nBound the cumulative artifact size under `--output-dir` during a real\neval run so a runaway suite cannot fill the host disk. The cliEval\ndesign-spec §4 / §13 (NFR-PERF4) commit the orchestrator to a five-\nsecond polling cadence and a default 1024 MB budget; design-spec §10\nrisk R4 documents the failure mode the poller mitigates (a 15-eval\nfan-out with PTY transcripts can grow past several hundred megabytes\non a slow eval and corrupt every neighbouring run).\n\nOn breach the harness must:\n\n1. Stays `True` for the lifetime of the poller. |\n| `breach_detail()` | `Mapping[str, object]` matching `BreachDetail.to_dict()`, or `None` while healthy. |\n| `artifact_path()` | `Path` of the side-car file once written, or `None`. |\n| `start()` | Spawn the background daemon thread. No-op when `max_disk_mb == 0` or the thread is already alive. |\n| `stop(*, timeout=None)` | Signal the thread to exit and `join` it. Idempotent. Does **not** clear the breach flag. |\n| `__enter__` / `__exit__` | Convenience context-manager form (`start` on enter, `stop` on exit). |\n\n### 2.2 `BreachDetail`\n\nFrozen dataclass serialised verbatim into the side-car JSON:\n\n| Field | Type | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `reason` | `str` | Always `DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_REASON`. |\n| `output_dir` | `str` | Absolute path of the watched directory. |\n| `usage_bytes` | `int` | Measured cumulative size at the breach tick. |\n| `budget_bytes` | `int` | `max_disk_mb * 1024 * 1024`. |\n| `max_disk_mb` | `int` | Operator-configured budget. |\n| `ticked_at` | `str` | ISO-8601 UTC (`Z`-suffixed) timestamp. |\n\n### 2.3 Side-car shape\n\nWritten to `output_dir / DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"budget_bytes\": 1073741824,\n  \"max_disk_mb\": 1024,\n  \"output_dir\": \"/tmp/run-xyz\",\n  \"reason\": \"disk_budget_exceeded\",\n  \"ticked_at\": \"2026-05-20T13:28:09Z\",\n  \"usage_bytes\": 1099773888\n}\n```\n\n`json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)` plus a trailing newline so\nthe file is review-friendly and round-trips through `jq`. Polling cadence & breach semantics\n\n```python\nwhile not self._stop_event.wait(self._tick_sec):\n    usage_bytes = self._compute_usage()\n    if usage_bytes > self._budget_bytes:\n        self._record_breach(usage_bytes)\n        return\n```\n\n* `threading.Event.wait(tick_sec)` is the cancellable sleep — `stop()`\n  short-circuits the next tick instead of waiting up to `tick_sec` for\n  the loop to notice.\n* First tick fires *after* the initial sleep so an empty run directory\n  does not trip the breach during start-up.\n* `_compute_usage` walks the output tree with `rglob('*')`, skips\n  symlinks (cannot be tricked into double-counting via a sibling-tree\n  link), and swallows `OSError` / `FileNotFoundError` (in-flight\n  runners reaping scratch files between `rglob` and `stat` must not\n  crash the poller).\n* On breach the poller writes the side-car, **publishes\n  `_detail` / `_artifact_path`, and only then sets `_breach_event`**\n  — release-then-set ordering so any consumer that observes\n  `is_breached() is True` is guaranteed a non-`None` `breach_detail()`\n  without explicit locking.\n* The breach flag is one-shot. Goal\n\nBound the cumulative artifact size under `--output-dir` during a real\neval run so a runaway suite cannot fill the host disk. The cliEval\ndesign-spec §4 / §13 (NFR-PERF4) commit the orchestrator to a five-\nsecond polling cadence and a default 1024 MB budget; design-spec §10\nrisk R4 documents the failure mode the poller mitigates (a 15-eval\nfan-out with PTY transcripts can grow past several hundred megabytes\non a slow eval and corrupt every neighbouring run).\n\nOn breach the harness must:\n\n1. Stop scheduling new evals.\n2. Allow in-flight evals to complete (no thread-kill).\n3. Exit `2` (harness error) with a `disk_budget_exceeded.json` side-car\n   the Reporter surfaces under `RunSummary.artifacts`.\n\n## 2. Public Surface\n\n```python\nfrom superclaude.cli.eval.disk_budget import (\n    DEFAULT_DISK_BUDGET_MB,             # 1024\n    DEFAULT_DISK_POLL_TICK_SEC,         # 5.0\n    DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME, # \"disk_budget_exceeded.json\"\n    DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE,     # 2\n    DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_REASON,        # \"disk_budget_exceeded\"\n    BreachDetail,\n    DiskBudgetPoller,\n)\n```\n\n### 2.1 `DiskBudgetPoller`\n\n| Attribute / method | Contract |\n|---|---|\n| `__init__(output_dir, *, max_disk_mb=1024, tick_sec=5.0, artifact_name=..., ensure_output_dir=False, clock=None)` | Construct the poller. `max_disk_mb < 0` → `ValueError`; non-`int` (or `bool`) → `TypeError`; `tick_sec ≤ 0` → `ValueError`. |\n| `enabled` | `True` when `max_disk_mb > 0`. |\n| `max_disk_mb`, `budget_bytes`, `tick_sec`, `output_dir`, `artifact_name` | Read-only configuration accessors. |\n| `is_breached()` | One-shot flag flipped by the polling thread on the first breach. Stays `True` for the lifetime of the poller. |\n| `breach_detail()` | `Mapping[str, object]` matching `BreachDetail.to_dict()`, or `None` while healthy. |\n| `artifact_path()` | `Path` of the side-car file once written, or `None`. |\n| `start()` | Spawn the background daemon thread. No-op when `max_disk_mb == 0` or the thread is already alive. |\n| `stop(*, timeout=None)` | Signal the thread to exit and `join` it. Idempotent. Does **not** clear the breach flag. |\n| `__enter__` / `__exit__` | Convenience context-manager form (`start` on enter, `stop` on exit). |\n\n### 2.2 `BreachDetail`\n\nFrozen dataclass serialised verbatim into the side-car JSON:\n\n| Field | Type | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `reason` | `str` | Always `DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_REASON`. |\n| `output_dir` | `str` | Absolute path of the watched directory. |\n| `usage_bytes` | `int` | Measured cumulative size at the breach tick. |\n| `budget_bytes` | `int` | `max_disk_mb * 1024 * 1024`. |\n| `max_disk_mb` | `int` | Operator-configured budget. |\n| `ticked_at` | `str` | ISO-8601 UTC (`Z`-suffixed) timestamp. |\n\n### 2.3 Side-car shape\n\nWritten to `output_dir / DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"budget_bytes\": 1073741824,\n  \"max_disk_mb\": 1024,\n  \"output_dir\": \"/tmp/run-xyz\",\n  \"reason\": \"disk_budget_exceeded\",\n  \"ticked_at\": \"2026-05-20T13:28:09Z\",\n  \"usage_bytes\": 1099773888\n}\n```\n\n`json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)` plus a trailing newline so\nthe file is review-friendly and round-trips through `jq`. The Reporter\n(COMP-008) surfaces the path under\n`RunSummary.artifacts[\"disk_budget_exceeded\"]`.\n\n## 3. Polling cadence & breach semantics\n\n```python\nwhile not self._stop_event.wait(self._tick_sec):\n    usage_bytes = self._compute_usage()\n    if usage_bytes > self._budget_bytes:\n        self._record_breach(usage_bytes)\n        return\n```\n\n* `threading.Event.wait(tick_sec)` is the cancellable sleep — `stop()`\n  short-circuits the next tick instead of waiting up to `tick_sec` for\n  the loop to notice.\n* First tick fires *after* the initial sleep so an empty run directory\n  does not trip the breach during start-up.\n* `_compute_usage` walks the output tree with `rglob('*')`, skips\n  symlinks (cannot be tricked into double-counting via a sibling-tree\n  link), and swallows `OSError` / `FileNotFoundError` (in-flight\n  runners reaping scratch files between `rglob` and `stat` must not\n  crash the poller).\n* On breach the poller writes the side-car, **publishes\n  `_detail` / `_artifact_path`, and only then sets `_breach_event`**\n  — release-then-set ordering so any consumer that observes\n  `is_breached() is True` is guaranteed a non-`None` `breach_detail()`\n  without explicit locking.\n* The breach flag is one-shot. Once set, deleting the offending\n  payload does not clear it; the orchestrator sees a stable signal\n  for the rest of the run.\n\n`max_disk_mb == 0` disables the poller entirely: `start()` is a no-op,\nno thread is spawned, `is_breached()` always returns `False`. Design-\nspec §4 documents this as the \"disable the budget\" invocation.\n\n## 4. Orchestrator Integration\n\n`RunOrchestrator.__init__` accepts `disk_budget_poller:\nOptional[DiskBudgetPoller] = None`. When wired:\n\n```python\npoller = self._disk_budget_poller\nif poller is not None:\n    poller.start()\ntry:\n    with ThreadPoolExecutor(...) as pool:\n        for index, spec in enumerate(specs):\n            if self._is_cancelled():\n                cancelled_indices.append(index)\n                continue\n            if self._is_disk_budget_exceeded():\n                disk_budget_skipped_indices.append(index)\n                continue\n            futures[pool.submit(self._invoke_worker, spec)] = index\n        for future in as_completed(futures):\n            ...\nfinally:\n    if poller is not None:\n        poller.stop()\n\nfor index in cancelled_indices:\n    outcomes[index] = self._interrupted_outcome(specs[index])\nfor index in disk_budget_skipped_indices:\n    outcomes[index] = self._disk_budget_skipped_outcome(specs[index])\n```\n\nThe synthesised SKIPPED outcome carries:\n\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| `status` | `\"SKIPPED\"` |\n| `skip_reason` | `DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_REASON` (`\"disk_budget_exceeded\"`) |\n| `skip_flag_triggered` | `\"--max-disk-mb\"` |\n| `expects` | `()` |\n| `artifacts` | `{}` |\n| `duration_sec` | `0.0` |\n\nPriority: cancellation dominates a disk-budget breach when both fire\nin the same submission iteration (operator intent overrides a\nresource limit). Test:\n`TestOrchestratorIntegration::test_cancellation_takes_priority_over_disk_breach`.\n\nIn-flight workers run to completion. The orchestrator never kills a\nworker thread — `as_completed` still drains the pool before `stop()`\njoins the poller. Test:\n`TestOrchestratorIntegration::test_inflight_workers_complete_after_breach`.\n\n## 5. Out of Scope\n\n* **CLI flag wiring.** The Phase 4 dispatcher binds `--max-disk-mb`\n  to the constructor and maps `DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE = 2`\n  to the process exit status. This deliverable owns the primitive,\n  not the dispatch.\n* **Reporter side-car surfacing.** COMP-008 / T03.13 read\n  `output_dir / DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_ARTIFACT_NAME` and stamp the\n  path into `RunSummary.artifacts[\"disk_budget_exceeded\"]`. The\n  poller only writes the file; it does not mutate the summary.\n* **Disk-space pre-flight checks.** The doctor command may grow a\n  pre-flight that warns when free space is low, but that lives\n  outside the polling loop.\n* **Per-eval scratch teardown after breach.** Workers continue to\n  use the HOME they already own; the harness does not reclaim disk\n  proactively on breach.\n\n## 6. Failure Modes & Containment\n\n| Mode | Behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| `max_disk_mb < 0` | `ValueError` from `__init__`. |\n| `max_disk_mb` not `int` (or `bool`) | `TypeError`. |\n| `tick_sec ≤ 0` | `ValueError`. |\n| `artifact_name == \"\"` | `ValueError`. |\n| `output_dir` does not exist | `_compute_usage` returns `0`; no breach. The poller silently waits until the orchestrator creates the directory. |\n| Filesystem unavailable on breach (write fails) | In-memory `BreachDetail` still published, `is_breached()` still flips, `artifact_path()` returns `None`. These notes capture the design decisions made\nwhile implementing T03.19 (NFR-PERF4 disk-budget poller), the\nalternatives considered, and the reasoning behind the chosen contract.\n\n## Why a separate breach `Event` instead of reusing `CancellationToken`\n\nThe first sketch reused the `CancellationToken` the orchestrator already\nthreads through `EvalRunner`. That was rejected because the AC requires\n\"in-flight evals **complete**\" — `CancellationToken` propagates to the\nin-runner `EvalRunner._cancellation_token` which converts in-flight\nwork into `INTERRUPTED` outcomes (D-0050). Sharing the token would\ntruncate the in-flight evals on breach, violating the AC.\n\nA dedicated `threading.Event` on the poller decouples the two signals:\n\n| Signal | Semantics | In-flight outcome shape |\n|---|---|---|\n| `CancellationToken.is_cancelled()` | Operator pressed Ctrl-C / SIGTERM | `INTERRUPTED` (runner aborts pty wait) |\n| `DiskBudgetPoller.is_breached()` | Disk budget exceeded | In-flight workers run to completion (`PASS` / `FAIL` / `TIMEOUT` per normal classification); only unsubmitted specs get `SKIPPED` |\n\nThe orchestrator polls both flags, but only the first one propagates\ninto the worker.\n\n## Why `SKIPPED` for unsubmitted specs (not `INTERRUPTED` / `ERRORED`)\n\nThree statuses were candidates:\n\n1. **`INTERRUPTED`** — semantically wrong: there was no interruption.\n   `INTERRUPTED` is reserved for operator-initiated cancellation\n   (SIGINT/SIGTERM). Reusing it here would conflate two distinct\n   exit paths and prevent the Reporter from distinguishing \"user\n   aborted\" from \"harness aborted on resource limit\".\n2. **`ERRORED`** — close, but `ERRORED` is for harness errors during\n   eval execution (D-0049 lifecycle phases). The spec never ran, so\n   there was nothing to error on.\n3. **`SKIPPED`** — the natural fit. DM-001 already pairs `SKIPPED`\n   with `skip_reason` and `skip_flag_triggered`, which are exactly\n   the fields needed to surface the disk-budget abort. The Reporter\n   can match on `skip_reason == \"disk_budget_exceeded\"` without\n   parsing free-form text, and the `--max-disk-mb` flag is named\n   explicitly via `skip_flag_triggered`.\n\nThe `DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_REASON` constant pins the token so consumers\ndo not have to discover it by string-matching.\n\n## Why `threading.Event.wait(tick_sec)` instead of `time.sleep`\n\n`time.sleep` is uninterruptible — `stop()` would have to wait up to\n`tick_sec` seconds before the next loop iteration noticed the stop\nflag. `Event.wait(tick_sec)` returns immediately when `set()` is\ncalled from another thread, so `stop()` is responsive even with the\n5-second production cadence.\n\nThe boolean return of `wait` is exploited directly: `while not\nself._stop_event.wait(self._tick_sec):` is the cleanest expression of\n\"sleep `tick_sec`, exit if stop was requested\".\n\n## Why release-then-set ordering for breach publication\n\nThe reader (orchestrator main thread) calls `is_breached()` and then,\non `True`, may call `breach_detail()`. Without ordering, the reader\ncould observe the flag without observing the detail.\n\nPattern:\n\n```python\n# In poller thread:\nself._detail = detail               # publish first\nself._artifact_path = artifact_path\nself._breach_event.set()            # then flip the flag\n\n# In orchestrator thread:\nif poller.is_breached():            # observe the flag\n    detail = poller.breach_detail() # detail is guaranteed populated\n```\n\nThis is the standard release-store / acquire-load idiom adapted to\nPython's `threading.Event` (which uses a `Condition` internally with\nthe implicit memory barriers of `Lock`). The reader observes the\ndetail via plain attribute access; the event provides the\nsynchronisation. No explicit lock is needed in the reader path\nbecause the detail is only ever written once before the flag flips\nand is never mutated thereafter.\n\n## Why skip symlinks in the disk walk\n\nTwo attack vectors motivated this:\n\n1. **Sibling-tree double-counting.** A symlink under `output_dir`\n   pointing at a sibling tree would inflate the usage measurement\n   relative to the actual on-disk footprint, triggering false-positive\n   breaches.\n2. **Cross-mount escape.** A symlink to `/var` (or another large\n   filesystem) would let an unrelated file inflate the measurement\n   and crash a healthy run.\n\nSkipping symlinks entirely (rather than resolving them and de-\nduplicating) is the simplest defensible policy: the poller measures\nexactly what is allocated under the output tree, no more and no less.\nA test (`TestSymlinkHandling::test_symlinks_are_skipped`) pins the\nbehaviour against regressions.\n\n## Why swallow per-file `OSError` instead of crashing the poller\n\nProduction scenarios that produce transient `OSError` during the walk:\n\n- A runner's scratch HOME is reaped between `rglob` and `stat`.\n- The orchestrator deletes a partial artifact during teardown.\n- The poller races a `Path.unlink()` from a finishing worker.\n\nA poller that crashes on a transient missing file is worse than no\npoller: the orchestrator never sees the breach flag flip and disk\nkeeps growing. Swallowing the error lets the next tick re-measure\ncorrectly. The trade-off — that a corrupted filesystem returning\n`EIO` consistently would silently produce `0`-byte usage — is\ndocumented in the spec failure-mode table.\n\n## Why `max_disk_mb == 0` is the disable sentinel (not `None`)\n\nThree reasons:\n\n1. **CLI ergonomics.** `--max-disk-mb 0` reads as \"no budget\" in shell\n   syntax. `--max-disk-mb=None` is not a thing in Click; using `None`\n   would force a separate `--no-disk-budget` flag.\n2. **Constant type stability.** `DEFAULT_DISK_BUDGET_MB: int = 1024`\n   stays an `int`. A sentinel `None` would force the type to\n   `Optional[int]` everywhere and add `None` checks throughout the\n   orchestrator.\n3. **`start()` no-op idempotency.** The orchestrator can call\n   `poller.start()` unconditionally; the disabled poller silently\n   declines to spawn a thread. The integration code stays clean of\n   conditional branching.\n\n## Why cancellation dominates breach in the submission loop\n\nThe submission loop checks cancellation first, then disk budget:\n\n```python\nif self._is_cancelled():\n    cancelled_indices.append(index)\n    continue\nif self._is_disk_budget_exceeded():\n    disk_budget_skipped_indices.append(index)\n    continue\n```\n\nIf both fire simultaneously (operator presses Ctrl-C while disk is\nalready over budget), the spec is routed to `INTERRUPTED`. The\nrationale is operator-intent precedence: a Ctrl-C is a deliberate\nchoice to stop, so the outcome should reflect *why the operator\naborted*, not the underlying resource state. The Reporter can still\ninspect the side-car JSON to learn that the disk was also breached.\n\nTest: `TestOrchestratorIntegration::test_cancellation_takes_priority_over_disk_breach`.\n\n## Why no `--max-disk-mb` wiring in this deliverable\n\nThe poller is the primitive; the CLI flag is the dispatcher's\nresponsibility (Phase 4). Two reasons for the split:\n\n1. **Scope discipline.** D-0060 owns the polling primitive and the\n   orchestrator integration. Flag parsing and exit-code translation\n   are CLI-shape concerns that change independently.\n2. **Reusability.** A future component (eg. the `doctor` pre-flight,\n   T03.06 follow-up) may want the polling primitive without the\n   `--max-disk-mb` flag wiring. Keeping the primitive standalone\n   makes that re-use trivial.\n\nThe `DISK_BUDGET_EXCEEDED_EXIT_CODE` constant lives in `disk_budget`\nso the Phase 4 dispatcher has one obvious import target.\n\n## Why a side-car JSON file instead of writing into `summary.json`\n\n`summary.json` (DM-012) is written by the Reporter at the end of the\nrun from the in-memory `RunSummary`. The poller runs concurrently\nwith the orchestrator and must record the breach *before* the\nReporter assembles the summary — otherwise a crash between the\nbreach and the summary write would lose the diagnostic.\n\nThe side-car is independent of the Reporter's success and survives\nprocess crash. The Reporter then reads the file at summary-assembly\ntime and stamps the path into `RunSummary.artifacts[\"disk_budget_exceeded\"]`.\n\n## Reference implementation\n\n- Pattern source: `src/superclaude/cli/eval/orchestrator.py` D-0057\n  scheduling loop (same `ThreadPoolExecutor + as_completed` shape\n  the integration extends).\n- Companion: D-0050 cancellation token + `INTERRUPTED` synthesis\n  pattern (mirrored for `SKIPPED` synthesis here).\n\n## Verification evidence\n\nSee `evidence.md` in this directory.
